headline: CRUDE BREAKS 5.6%; BEANS WAIT FOR XI
lead: Saudi Aramco's Gulf reroute -- started this week after the East-West pipeline shifted 60 million barrels back through the Persian Gulf -- knocked crude down 5.6% to **$95.47**, its biggest single-session drop in months. Relief, not shortage, is what the market priced Friday. Diesel harvest risk hasn't left; it just got cheaper to ignore.
teaser: Saudi crude reroute tanks oil; beans sell off as traders wait on Xi.

one_number.context: Tightest feeder supply in the data series. The Cargill lockout is processing-constrained; this says the supply side is tightening too, which keeps the feeder market's floor intact.

yesterdays_call.note: Miss; beans fell 7½ cents to $13.03, stopping 39 cents short of the line and closing at a session low.
yesterdays_call.call_line: Called soybeans up toward $13.42 ($13.2625 when the call was made). It closed at $13.03.

action: Unpriced new-crop beans: hold through the weekend. A Monday settle above $13.10 is the first reason to price anything before the Xi summit.

sections.title: CRUDE BREAKS; ENERGY LEADS LOWER
sections.body: - WTI fell to **$95.47**, a 5.6% drop, after Saudi Aramco confirmed the East-West pipeline reroute is moving roughly 60 million barrels back through the Persian Gulf, cutting Europe off from October deliveries but easing the supply-shortage selling pressure that ran crude higher all week.
sections.so_what: Crude relief is real; diesel tightness for harvest is not over.

sections.title: BEANS WAIT FOR XI
sections.body: - Soybeans fell to **$13.03**, down 7½ cents, as funds liquidated ahead of the September 24 Trump-Xi summit where, per ASA, the 10% retaliatory soybean levy and China's purchase commitments are both on the table under China's $17 billion annual US ag purchase deal.
sections.so_what: Beans are hostage to one calendar event; the price reflects that honestly.

sections.title: CATTLE HOLD; FEEDERS SLIP
sections.body: - Live cattle firmed to **$216.57**, up 0.2%, a quiet session; the Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19 and still removing roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity, keeps the processing constraint in place and gives live cattle a floor.
sections.so_what: Record-low placements backstop feeders even as the border reopens.

outside_the_pit.title: Farm Bill Clears Senate Ag After Weeks of Gridlock
outside_the_pit.body: The Senate Ag Committee advanced the 2026 Farm Bill 12-11 on a party-line vote Wednesday. Floor fights remain and the September 30 extension deadline is two weeks out.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress: corn harvest pace above 15% keeps harvest pressure on; below 10% limits it.
Trump-Xi summit: any soybean levy reduction is the catalyst beans have been pricing around all week.
September WASDE: corn carryout below 1.6 billion bushels would be the next leg of the corn rally.
